html:
A significant escalation in the US-Iran war is unfolding today, marked by a drone attack in Kuwait that killed two Italians, an incident Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi called "suspicious" and a "pre-cooked recipe" for war, while Tehran denies involvement and Syria condemns the attack. This comes as a US naval blockade continues to pressure Iran's economy, with Iranian economists warning its effects are not fully offset.

Middle East Security: Iran's military has reported two more oil tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines, with one violating maritime regulations. Iran’s Army spokesperson says the military has tightened security measures in the Strait, warning vessels to coordinate passage. Meanwhile, Trump praised US troops for their role in the war on Iran and said he has spoken to Netanyahu in recent days, while downplaying Russia and China's support for Iran. Italy's Meloni expressed sorrow for the deaths of Italian nationals in Kuwait. Iran is also rapidly constructing an underground complex near nuclear sites and developing new ballistic missile variants, with a nuclear chief stating Iran will not stop nuclear progress, as Iran-backed Iraqi militia reportedly prepare for a renewed US-Iran war.

Russia-Ukraine Conflict: Ukraine's president Zelensky voiced frustration with the US, telling the BBC it is too focused on the Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, also questioning Trump's description of Vladimir Putin as a friend. Trump and a NATO chief have urged Russia not to "expand" the Ukraine war, as Kyiv intensifies pressure on Moscow by attacking Russian vessels around the world. In response to a rising Russia threat, the UK is undertaking a "Cold War-scale push" by shielding fighter jets and contacting reservists. White House envoy Jared Kushner commented that Vladimir Putin has "shown restraint" by not using nuclear weapons in the conflict.

Global Economy & Europe: European leaders have nominated Pablo Hernandez de Cos, the former head of the Bank of Spain, as the next ECB president, replacing Christine Lagarde, as the bank faces pressure to tackle high inflation and borrowing costs. Meanwhile, Black Friday has become a truly global phenomenon. In Spain, a snap election on Sunday is accompanied by allegations of vote rigging, with the far right gaining ground. Americans face higher costs for Thanksgiving celebrations and are expected to spend nearly $1 billion more on gas, a reminder of elevated pump prices due to the Iran war.

Other Conflicts & Security: In Gaza, Israeli strikes killed 10 Palestinians, including a Hamas political official, prompting Hamas to say it is weighing its options against Israel, while the US urged Netanyahu to proceed with a ceasefire plan. Netanyahu also demanded an immediate end to his corruption trial. In North Korea, Kim Jong Un has vowed to build more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the US and South Korea, ignoring Trump's overture. The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a Houthi drone and a projectile near Jeddah and Jazan ports, with one worker killed after the Jazan refinery was hit. A fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has reached 12,000 cases, with responders evacuating due to ongoing fighting between rebels and the army.

Domestic Politics & Governance: New Zealand's right-leaning ruling coalition led by the National Party has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, leading to a deadlocked final result. China has launched an investigation into Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining as part of President Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign. Bangladesh is on edge over the planned return of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who faces a death sentence. Albanian youth are protesting against a rigid political system and corruption in what is termed the "Flamingo Revolution."
